title: Canonical higher cohomology comparison across a dense open
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a separated finite-type scheme of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative ring and $F$ any sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For a dense open $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, let $G=j_!j^*F$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], and let $\epsilon:G\to F$ be the counit [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], viewed as a morphism of underlying abelian sheaves. Then the canonical map $H^q(\epsilon):H^q(X,G)\to H^q(X,F)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] is bijective for every $q>1$. Moreover, for every open immersion $a:W\to X$, the map $H^2(a^*\epsilon):H^2(W,a^*G)\to H^2(W,a^*F)$ is bijective. No torsion, constructibility or reducedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof: the isomorphisms for q>1 and remark (d)

proof.text: Let Z be the reduced closed complement of U. Finite type makes X Noetherian with finitely many irreducible components. Density and openness put the generic point of every component in U: if its closure meets U, every generalization of that point of intersection lies in U. Thus no irreducible component lies in Z. Any strict chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets in Z would extend by a component of X to a chain of length at least two in X, contradicting dimension at most one. Hence Z has dimension at most zero. Its underlying space is finite and discrete, and each residue field is k. The same argument applies to any open immersion W into X and the complement W times_X Z.

The open-closed short exact sequence of module sheaves is 0 -> G -> F -> i_*i^*F -> 0, with the first arrow the specified adjunction counit. Forgetting module structure gives a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves. Finite exact direct image and the Leray identification give H^q(X,i_*i^*F)=H^q(Z,i^*F). This vanishes for q>0. Inverse image along any open immersion is exact and computes the analogous closed direct image over the intersection with Z.

In the long exact sequence, the kernel and cokernel of H^q(G) -> H^q(F) for q>1 are controlled by H^{q-1}(i_*i^*F) and H^q(i_*i^*F), both zero. Therefore Sheaf.H.map of the forgotten counit is bijective. Apply the pulled-back sequence on each open W in degree two to obtain bijectivity of Sheaf.H.map of the pulled-back counit. Naturality identifies these maps with the maps written in the Lean statement.
Empty X, empty complement, and arbitrary nonconstructible or nontorsion coefficients cause no change: only positive-degree vanishing on the finite union of algebraically closed points was used.

theorem dense_open_high_cohomology (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set X)) :
    let ε := (sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology
      (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).map
        ((openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) U.ι).counit.app F)
    (∀ q : ℕ, 1 < q → Function.Bijective (Sheaf.H.map ε q)) ∧
      (∀ {W : Scheme.{u}} (a : W ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion a],
        Function.Bijective
          (Sheaf.H.map (((a)^*[AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]).map ε) 2))
